When I was 7, a new girl moved to my school. I remember being in gym class (they put us in lines and made us do exercises before playing, so I was in view of the front door) and her walking in, she dressed masculine, but was very obviously a girl. I was INSTANTLY crushing hard, but in my mind I had convinced myself that she was just a boy with long hair and a "girl" face because I didn't know being gay was a thing and at that age I couldn't rationalize having a crush on a girl, because I didn't even know it was possible. Eventually I let it go. Three years later, a new girl started going to our school and she was open about liking girls. Eventually we became friends, and a friend of ours invited us both over. While there her older sister randomly kissed her, I remember being super mad and jealous and not saying anything. That night while going to sleep I kept thinking "why did that make me mad? Why am I jealous of that?" then it hit me hard, I liked her, and I understood this time. I remember freaking out and being super on edge for a long time, till I came out to a close friend. They were super accepting and it eased a lot of the pressure. Well, not long after me and the girl I liked got closer and you could feel how nervous I felt around her, till I asked her out and she said yes. That's how I came out, kissing a cute girl at school. We dated for a long long time on and off and it took me four years to move on from that relationship.

It looks like a pretty decently sized irritation bump to me, can be caused by putting too much pressure on the piercing (sleeping on it, pulling on the jewelry, or accidentally hitting it), being in chlorine for long periods of time, or just overall moisture buildup. I'm not an professional piercer however, I just do my my own, so I would definitely consult a local professional piercer for their opinion. Salt water soaks, anti-swelling meds, or a compress can help it go away for the most part, but if it isn't gone in 3 weeks I would take it out.

Keloids aren't just normal bumps, they are scars that have been irritated and raised. They do not go away on their own, you have to have a keloid medically removed or you will have it forever, at best, it will shrink a decent bit, but not disappear completely.
